domain: Snowflake AI Data Cloud Features & Architecture

questions.question: Snowflake's architecture is described as a hybrid of which two architecture models?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Snowflake uses a hybrid architecture combining shared-disk (centralized storage accessible by all compute nodes) and shared-nothing (each compute node processes queries independently using local caching). B, C, and D do not accurately describe Snowflake's architectural model.

questions.question: Which three distinct layers make up Snowflake's architecture?

options.text: Presentation Layer, Application Layer, Data Layer
Database Storage, Query Processing (Virtual Warehouses), Cloud Services
Ingestion Layer, Compute Layer, Output Layer
Client Layer, Middleware Layer, Database Layer

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake's three layers are: Database Storage (stores data in micro-partitions), Query Processing (virtual warehouses that execute queries), and Cloud Services (handles authentication, metadata, optimization, and infrastructure management).

questions.question: In Snowflake, data is stored in which format?

options.text: Row-based format similar to traditional databases
Key-value pairs in distributed hash tables

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores data in a proprietary columnar format within compressed micro-partitions. Each micro-partition is 50-500MB of uncompressed data, stored compressed in cloud storage. This columnar approach enables efficient query processing and compression.

questions.question: What is the typical uncompressed size range of a Snowflake micro-partition?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake micro-partitions contain 50 to 500 MB of uncompressed data. They are organized in a columnar format and automatically compressed, enabling efficient storage and query pruning. The other ranges are incorrect.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake's Cloud Services layer is TRUE?

options.text: It manages infrastructure, metadata, authentication, and query optimization
It is responsible for data compression and encryption only

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Cloud Services layer handles authentication, access control, infrastructure management, metadata management, query parsing, and optimization. A is wrong — query execution happens in the Query Processing layer. C is wrong — storage is the Database Storage layer.

questions.question: What happens when you resize a virtual warehouse from X-Small to Small?

options.text: All running queries are terminated and restarted on the new size
The warehouse must be suspended before resizing
Running queries continue on the current size; new queries use the new size
The resize is queued until all current queries finish

questions.explanation: C is correct. When you resize a warehouse, existing queries continue running with the current compute resources. New queries submitted after the resize will use the new warehouse size. There is no need to suspend the warehouse or wait for queries to finish.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition is required to use multi-cluster warehouses?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Multi-cluster warehouses require Enterprise Edition or higher. Standard Edition does not support multi-cluster warehouses. Business Critical and VPS also support them, but Enterprise is the minimum required edition.

questions.question: How are virtual warehouses billed in Snowflake?

options.text: Per-minute with a minimum of 60 seconds
Per-second with a minimum of 60 seconds
Per-hour with a minimum of 30 minutes

questions.explanation: B is correct. Virtual warehouses are billed per-second with a minimum charge of 60 seconds each time they are resumed. This means if a warehouse runs for 65 seconds, you are charged for 65 seconds. If it runs for 30 seconds, you are charged for 60 seconds (the minimum).

questions.question: What is the recommended best practice for AUTO_SUSPEND on a virtual warehouse?

options.text: Set AUTO_SUSPEND = 0 to keep warehouses always running
Set AUTO_SUSPEND between 60 and 600 seconds depending on workload
Never use AUTO_SUSPEND; always manually suspend warehouses
Set AUTO_SUSPEND = 3600 (1 hour) for all warehouses

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake recommends setting AUTO_SUSPEND between 60 seconds and 600 seconds depending on whether you need to keep the warehouse cache warm. Setting it to 0 means the warehouse never auto-suspends, which wastes credits. Manual suspension is impractical for most workloads.

questions.question: How frequently does Snowflake release new versions of its software?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake releases new software versions on a weekly basis. These updates are applied transparently to all accounts without downtime, which is one advantage of the Snowflake SaaS model.

questions.question: Which cloud platforms does Snowflake currently support? (Choose three)
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. Snowflake runs natively on AWS, Azure, and GCP. It does not run on IBM Cloud or Oracle Cloud. Users can choose their cloud provider and region when creating a Snowflake account.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Snowflake's metadata store in the Cloud Services layer?

options.text: To store actual table data for fast retrieval
To track micro-partition statistics, file references, and table structure information
To cache query results for all users
To manage virtual warehouse configurations only

questions.explanation: B is correct. The metadata store tracks information about every micro-partition including min/max values, null counts, and the number of distinct values. This metadata enables query pruning, which skips irrelevant micro-partitions during query execution.

questions.question: Which of the following virtual warehouse sizes has the most compute resources?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Snowflake warehouse sizes range from X-Small to 6X-Large. Each increase in size doubles the compute resources and cost. 6X-Large is the largest available size with the most compute power.

questions.question: When a virtual warehouse size increases by one step (e.g., Small to Medium), what happens to the number of compute resources?

options.text: They increase by a variable amount

questions.explanation: B is correct. Each increase in warehouse size doubles the compute resources (servers/nodes) and correspondingly doubles the credit consumption per hour. For example, X-Small uses 1 credit/hour, Small uses 2, Medium uses 4, and so on.

questions.question: What is the credit consumption per hour for an X-Small virtual warehouse?
questions.explanation: B is correct. An X-Small warehouse consumes 1 credit per hour. Small = 2, Medium = 4, Large = 8, X-Large = 16, 2X-Large = 32, 3X-Large = 64, 4X-Large = 128 credits per hour.

questions.question: Which Snowflake component is responsible for executing SQL queries?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Virtual warehouses in the Query Processing layer are responsible for executing SQL queries. The Cloud Services layer handles query parsing and optimization but delegates execution to virtual warehouses. The Storage layer stores data but doesn't process queries.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition provides the highest level of security including HIPAA and PCI DSS compliance?
questions.explanation: D is correct. While Business Critical supports HIPAA and PCI DSS compliance, Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS) provides the highest level of security with a completely dedicated and isolated environment. VPS includes all Business Critical features plus dedicated metadata storage and isolated compute.

questions.question: Which Snowflake feature allows you to access data stored in external cloud storage without loading it into Snowflake?
questions.explanation: B is correct. External tables allow you to query data stored in external cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob, GCS) without loading it into Snowflake. Data Sharing shares Snowflake-native data between accounts. Internal stages are for loading data. Materialized views are pre-computed query results.

questions.question: What is Snowflake's approach to managing hardware and software updates?

options.text: Users must schedule maintenance windows for updates
Updates require a brief period of downtime
Snowflake is a SaaS platform; updates are applied transparently with no downtime
Users can choose to delay updates for up to 6 months

questions.explanation: C is correct. As a fully managed SaaS platform, Snowflake handles all hardware and software updates transparently. There is no downtime required, no maintenance windows to schedule, and users benefit from the latest features automatically.

questions.question: What is the Snowflake object hierarchy from top to bottom?
questions.explanation: A is correct. The Snowflake hierarchy is: Organization (top level, can contain multiple accounts) → Account → Database → Schema → Objects (tables, views, etc.). This hierarchical structure organizes all Snowflake resources.

questions.question: Which connector is Snowflake's command-line client for executing SQL?
questions.explanation: A is correct. SnowSQL is Snowflake's command-line client for executing SQL queries and performing DDL/DML operations. Snowpipe is for continuous data loading. SnowCD is a connectivity diagnostic tool. Snowsight is the web-based UI.

questions.question: What is Snowsight?

options.text: A command-line tool for managing Snowflake accounts
Snowflake's web-based user interface for querying, visualization, and administration
A data integration tool for ETL pipelines
A third-party monitoring tool for Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowsight is Snowflake's modern web-based user interface. It provides SQL editing, query results visualization with charts, dashboards, worksheet sharing, and administrative capabilities — all through a browser.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid Snowflake connectors/drivers? (Choose three)
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. Snowflake provides JDBC, ODBC, and Python connectors natively, along with Node.js, .NET, Go, and PHP drivers. There are no native Redis or MongoDB connectors provided by Snowflake.

questions.question: In Snowflake, what determines how data is organized within micro-partitions?

options.text: Users must manually define partition keys
Data is automatically partitioned based on the insertion order
Data is partitioned based on a hash of the primary key
Data is randomly distributed across partitions

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake automatically organizes data into micro-partitions based on the natural insertion order. Users do not need to define partition keys. While clustering keys can be applied to reorganize data for performance, the default behavior is automatic partitioning by insertion order.

questions.question: What type of storage does Snowflake use for its Database Storage layer?

options.text: Local SSD storage on compute nodes
Cloud object storage (e.g., S3, Azure Blob, GCS)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores all table data in cloud object storage provided by the underlying cloud platform (Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage). Local SSD on compute nodes is used only for caching, not permanent storage.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake virtual warehouses is TRUE?

options.text: Multiple warehouses can share the same compute resources
Each virtual warehouse is an independent compute cluster that does not share resources with other warehouses
Warehouses must be manually provisioned and cannot auto-scale
A single warehouse is shared by all users in an account

questions.explanation: B is correct. Each virtual warehouse is an independent MPP compute cluster with dedicated resources. Warehouses do not compete with each other for compute resources, which is a key advantage of Snowflake's shared-nothing compute architecture.

questions.question: Which Snowflake feature enables automatic scaling of compute clusters to handle varying concurrency loads?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Multi-cluster warehouses can automatically scale out additional clusters to handle increased concurrency. Auto-resume starts a suspended warehouse. Warehouse resizing changes the size of the warehouse (vertically). Query acceleration offloads portions of queries to shared compute.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the scaling policy on a multi-cluster warehouse?

options.text: To control when additional clusters are started and shut down
To set the maximum number of queries per cluster

questions.explanation: B is correct. The scaling policy (STANDARD or ECONOMY) controls how aggressively Snowflake starts and shuts down additional clusters. STANDARD starts clusters more aggressively to minimize queuing. ECONOMY conserves credits by only starting new clusters when queries would be queued.

questions.question: Which scaling policy for multi-cluster warehouses prioritizes minimizing credit usage over minimizing query queuing time?
questions.explanation: B is correct. The ECONOMY scaling policy conserves credits by only starting additional clusters when enough queries are queued to keep a cluster busy for at least 6 minutes. STANDARD is more aggressive and starts clusters immediately when queuing begins. CONSERVATIVE and AGGRESSIVE are not valid policy names.

questions.question: Which Snowflake feature can be used to monitor and control credit usage for virtual warehouses?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Resource Monitors allow you to set credit quotas on warehouses and take actions (notify, suspend, suspend immediately) when thresholds are reached. Query Profile is for analyzing query execution plans. Data Sharing is for sharing data between accounts.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition is required for database failover and failback?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Database failover and failback are available starting with the Business Critical edition. Standard and Enterprise editions support database replication but not failover/failback.

questions.question: Snowflake uses which approach for concurrency handling?

options.text: No concurrency control; queries are serialized

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake uses MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control), meaning readers never block writers and writers never block readers. Each query sees a consistent snapshot of the data as of the time the query started.

questions.question: Which data types does Snowflake use to store semi-structured data? (Choose three)
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. VARIANT can hold any type of data (including JSON, XML, Avro, etc.). OBJECT stores key-value pairs. ARRAY stores ordered lists. JSON and XML are data formats that can be stored in a VARIANT column, but they are not Snowflake data types.

questions.question: What happens when Snowflake's Cloud Services layer usage exceeds 10% of the daily warehouse compute usage?

options.text: Only the usage exceeding the 10% threshold is billed
The entire Cloud Services usage is billed
The account is suspended until the next billing cycle

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake provides a daily 10% adjustment where Cloud Services compute is not billed if it stays under 10% of daily warehouse compute. If it exceeds 10%, only the portion above the threshold is charged.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Snowflake Standard edition?

options.text: Automatic data replication for disaster recovery

questions.explanation: B is correct. Multi-cluster warehouses require Enterprise edition or higher. Standard edition includes 1 day of Time Travel, always-on encryption, and data replication. Multi-cluster warehouses are an Enterprise+ feature.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Snowflake's Query Acceleration Service?

options.text: To cache frequently run queries for faster execution
To offload portions of eligible queries to shared serverless compute resources
To automatically resize warehouses based on query complexity
To compress query results for faster transmission

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Query Acceleration Service (QAS) can accelerate parts of eligible queries by offloading work to serverless compute resources. It is particularly effective for queries that scan large amounts of data or have specific filter predicates.

questions.question: Snowflake supports which of the following as a native file format for loading and unloading data? (Choose three)
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. Snowflake natively supports CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet, ORC, and XML file formats. Excel (XLSX) and PDF are not supported as native load/unload formats.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Snowflake's approach to indexes?

options.text: Snowflake requires users to create indexes for optimal query performance
Snowflake does not use traditional indexes; it relies on micro-partition pruning and metadata
Snowflake automatically creates B-tree indexes on primary keys
Snowflake uses bitmap indexes on all columns

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake does not support or require traditional indexes. Instead, it uses micro-partition metadata (min/max values, distinct counts) to prune irrelevant partitions during query execution. This eliminates the overhead of index maintenance.

questions.question: What does the SHOW WAREHOUSES command display?

options.text: Current credit consumption for all warehouses
Properties and status of all warehouses the user has access to
Historical query performance on all warehouses
The internal architecture of each warehouse cluster

questions.explanation: B is correct. SHOW WAREHOUSES displays the properties (name, size, state, auto_suspend, auto_resume, etc.) and status of all warehouses that the current user has privileges to see. It does not show credit consumption details or query history.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between Snowflake accounts and cloud regions?

options.text: A Snowflake account can span multiple cloud regions simultaneously
Each Snowflake account is hosted in a single cloud region on a single cloud provider
All Snowflake accounts share the same global region
Snowflake accounts are region-agnostic and data is distributed globally

questions.explanation: B is correct. Each Snowflake account is provisioned in a specific cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and a specific region within that provider. To have presence in multiple regions, you need multiple accounts with database replication configured between them.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of databases that can be created in a single Snowflake account?

options.text: There is no hard limit; it is effectively unlimited

questions.explanation: C is correct. The default maximum number of databases per Snowflake account is 10,000. This includes permanent, transient, and temporary databases. This limit can be adjusted by contacting Snowflake support.

questions.question: Which statement about Snowflake's storage costs is correct?

options.text: Storage is billed based on the uncompressed size of the data
Storage is billed based on the average compressed size of data stored per month
Storage is free; you only pay for compute
Storage is billed per query based on data scanned

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake storage costs are based on the average amount of compressed data stored each month, including data in tables, Time Travel, and Fail-safe. Because Snowflake compresses data automatically, you pay for the compressed size, not the original uncompressed size.

questions.question: Snowflake stores data in an open file format that can be accessed directly by other tools.
questions.explanation: B is correct (False). Snowflake stores data in a proprietary, optimized columnar format. Data in Snowflake's internal storage cannot be directly accessed by external tools. You must use Snowflake's query engine (SQL) or unload data to access it.

questions.question: Which Snowflake feature allows sharing compute costs with data consumers who don't have a Snowflake account?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Reader Accounts (formerly Managed Accounts) allow data providers to create Snowflake accounts for consumers who don't have their own Snowflake account. The provider manages and pays for the reader account's compute costs. Direct Shares require consumers to have their own Snowflake account.

questions.question: What is Snowpark?

options.text: A developer framework that allows writing data pipelines in Python, Java, or Scala with dataframe-style APIs
A monitoring tool for warehouse performance

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowpark is a developer framework that lets you write data transformations and pipelines in Python, Java, or Scala using familiar dataframe-style APIs. Code executes within Snowflake's processing layer, enabling developers to work in their preferred language.

questions.question: What is the minimum Snowflake edition required for column-level security (Dynamic Data Masking)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Dynamic Data Masking is available starting with Enterprise edition. It allows you to define masking policies that conditionally mask sensitive column data at query time based on the user's role. Standard edition does not support this feature.

questions.question: What is the Snowflake Data Marketplace?

options.text: A platform for buying and selling Snowflake credits
A marketplace where data providers can publish datasets that consumers can access directly in their Snowflake accounts
An internal tool for managing database schemas
A tool for comparing pricing across cloud providers

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Snowflake Marketplace allows data providers to publish and monetize datasets. Data consumers can discover and access these datasets directly in their Snowflake accounts without any data copying or ETL required — data is accessed via Snowflake's secure data sharing.

questions.question: How does Snowflake handle data encryption?

options.text: Data is encrypted at rest only; in-transit encryption is optional
All data is encrypted at rest and in transit by default, with automatic key rotation
Encryption must be manually configured by the account administrator
Only Business Critical edition supports encryption

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake encrypts all data at rest using AES-256 encryption and all data in transit using TLS 1.2+. This encryption is automatic and enabled by default on all editions. Enterprise edition and above support periodic rekeying, and Business Critical supports customer-managed keys (Tri-Secret Secure).

questions.question: What is SnowCD used for?

options.text: Diagnosing and troubleshooting network connectivity to Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. SnowCD (Snowflake Connectivity Diagnostic Tool) is a command-line utility that checks network connectivity to Snowflake. It verifies that all required hosts and ports are accessible, which is useful for troubleshooting connection issues behind firewalls or proxies.

questions.question: Under what circumstances would you execute ALTER WAREHOUSE SET MIN_CLUSTER_COUNT = 1, MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT = 5?

options.text: You are executing queries that process terabytes of data and need more clusters to complete on time
There is a significant increase in concurrent users executing queries on the warehouse
Neither of the above is correct

questions.explanation: B is correct. Setting MIN_CLUSTER_COUNT and MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT configures multi-cluster warehouses to handle increased concurrency (more simultaneous users/queries). It does NOT improve performance for large individual queries — for that, you would resize the warehouse (increase its size).

questions.question: Which Snowflake layer is responsible for authentication, query parsing, optimization, and access control?
questions.explanation: C is correct. The Cloud Services Layer handles authentication, access control, query parsing/optimization, metadata management, infrastructure management, and transaction management. The Compute Layer executes queries, and the Storage Layer stores data.

questions.question: What type of storage does Snowflake use to store table data internally?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores data in columnar format within compressed micro-partitions. Each micro-partition contains 50-500 MB of uncompressed data. Columnar storage enables efficient query processing by reading only the columns needed.

questions.question: What is the approximate uncompressed size range of a Snowflake micro-partition?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Micro-partitions are between 50 and 500 MB of uncompressed data. They are automatically created and managed by Snowflake as data is inserted. Each micro-partition stores metadata about the data it contains for pruning optimization.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Query Tag parameter in Snowflake?

options.text: It specifies the warehouse to use for a query
It attaches a custom label to SQL statements for tracking, monitoring, and cost attribution
It tags tables with metadata categories
It assigns priority levels to queries

questions.explanation: B is correct. The QUERY_TAG session parameter lets you attach a custom string to all SQL statements in a session. This tag appears in QUERY_HISTORY and can be used for cost attribution, workload identification, and monitoring.

questions.question: In Snowflake, who manages the infrastructure (hardware, patching, upgrades)?

options.text: The customer is responsible for all infrastructure
Snowflake manages all infrastructure as a fully managed service
Infrastructure is shared between the customer and Snowflake

questions.explanation: C is correct. Snowflake is a fully managed SaaS platform. Snowflake handles all infrastructure management including hardware provisioning, software installation, patching, upgrades, and tuning. Customers focus only on loading and querying data.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a supported cloud platform for Snowflake?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Snowflake runs on AWS, Azure, and GCP. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is not a supported platform for Snowflake deployment.

questions.question: What metadata does Snowflake automatically store for each micro-partition?

options.text: Range of values for each column, number of distinct values, and NULL counts
Only the file size and creation date
Complete index of all values in every column

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores rich metadata for each micro-partition including the range of values (min/max) for each column, the number of distinct values, and NULL counts. This metadata enables efficient partition pruning without requiring manual indexes.

questions.question: Can two virtual warehouses access the same data simultaneously without contention?

options.text: No, one warehouse must wait for the other to finish
Yes, because compute and storage are separated
Only if they are in different accounts
Only if the data is replicated to both warehouses

questions.explanation: B is correct. Because Snowflake separates compute from storage, multiple warehouses can access the same data concurrently without any contention or performance impact on each other. Each warehouse has its own independent compute resources.

questions.question: What happens to a virtual warehouse's local disk cache when the warehouse is suspended?

options.text: The cache is dropped and must be rebuilt when resumed
The cache is saved to cloud storage
The cache is shared with other warehouses

questions.explanation: B is correct. When a warehouse is suspended, its compute resources (including local SSD cache) are released. When resumed, the cache starts empty and must be rebuilt as queries are executed. This is why the first queries after resuming may be slower.

questions.question: What is the default auto-suspend time for a virtual warehouse?
questions.explanation: B is correct. The default AUTO_SUSPEND setting is 600 seconds (10 minutes) of inactivity. After this period with no queries, the warehouse automatically suspends to save credits. This can be changed to any value from 0 (immediate) to any number of seconds.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Snowflake's approach to indexing?

options.text: Snowflake requires manual index creation for optimal performance
Snowflake uses automatic micro-partition pruning instead of traditional indexes
Snowflake uses B-tree indexes created during data loading
Snowflake does not support any form of data optimization

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake does not use traditional indexes. Instead, it leverages micro-partition metadata (min/max values per column) to prune partitions that don't contain relevant data. This eliminates the overhead of maintaining indexes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Snowflake's Information Schema?

options.text: A schema for storing user credentials
A set of system-defined views providing metadata about database objects (tables, views, columns, etc.) within a specific database
A schema for storing audit logs

questions.explanation: B is correct. Every Snowflake database automatically contains an INFORMATION_SCHEMA with system views like TABLES, COLUMNS, VIEWS, and TABLE_PRIVILEGES. Unlike ACCOUNT_USAGE (which has latency), Information Schema provides real-time metadata but only for the current database.

questions.question: What is Snowflake's Snowsight?

options.text: An ETL tool for data loading
Snowflake's web-based user interface for querying, visualization, and administration

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowsight is Snowflake's modern web-based UI that provides SQL worksheets, data visualization (dashboards and charts), administration features, activity monitoring, and collaboration capabilities.

questions.question: Which Snowflake connector allows direct integration with Apache Spark?
questions.explanation: B is correct. The Snowflake Connector for Spark enables bidirectional data transfer between Snowflake and Apache Spark. It pushes query processing to Snowflake when possible and supports reading/writing data between the two platforms.

questions.question: What is SnowSQL?

options.text: Snowflake's command-line client for executing SQL and DDL/DML operations
A Python library for connecting to Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. SnowSQL is Snowflake's official command-line interface (CLI) that allows users to execute SQL queries, perform DDL/DML operations, and manage Snowflake objects from a terminal. It supports scripting and automation.

questions.question: How does Snowflake charge for cloud services layer usage?

options.text: Cloud services are charged only when usage exceeds 10% of daily warehouse consumption
A per-query fee for every query executed

questions.explanation: C is correct. Cloud services compute is included up to 10% of the daily warehouse compute consumption. If cloud services usage exceeds this 10% threshold, the overage is billed separately. Most customers do not exceed this limit.

questions.question: What is the difference between ACCOUNT_USAGE and INFORMATION_SCHEMA?

options.text: ACCOUNT_USAGE covers the entire account with up to 365 days of history but has latency; INFORMATION_SCHEMA is real-time but limited to the current database
INFORMATION_SCHEMA is for admins; ACCOUNT_USAGE is for developers
ACCOUNT_USAGE is only available in Enterprise edition

questions.explanation: B is correct. ACCOUNT_USAGE (in the shared SNOWFLAKE database) provides account-wide metadata with up to 365 days of history but has 45 minutes to 3 hours of latency. INFORMATION_SCHEMA provides real-time metadata but is scoped to its containing database and has shorter retention.

questions.question: Which virtual warehouse size is the smallest available in Snowflake?
questions.explanation: A is correct. X-Small is the smallest warehouse size. Warehouse sizes range from X-Small to 6X-Large, with each size doubling the compute resources and credits consumed per hour compared to the previous size.

questions.question: When you double the size of a virtual warehouse (e.g., from Small to Medium), what happens to the credit consumption per hour?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Each warehouse size increase doubles the compute resources and credits consumed. X-Small = 1 credit/hour, Small = 2, Medium = 4, Large = 8, X-Large = 16, and so on.

questions.question: What is the credit consumption per hour for an X-Small warehouse?
questions.explanation: B is correct. An X-Small warehouse consumes 1 credit per hour. Small = 2, Medium = 4, Large = 8, X-Large = 16, 2X-Large = 32, 3X-Large = 64, 4X-Large = 128, 5X-Large = 256, 6X-Large = 512.

questions.question: What are the two main categories of Snowflake costs?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Snowflake billing has two primary components: Compute (measured in credits for warehouse usage and cloud services) and Storage (billed per TB per month for data stored including Time Travel and Fail-safe). Data transfer costs may also apply for cross-region/cross-cloud transfers.

questions.question: What does the AUTO_RESUME setting control on a virtual warehouse?

options.text: Whether the warehouse automatically resizes based on load
Whether the warehouse automatically starts when a query is submitted to it
Whether the warehouse automatically refreshes its cache
Whether the warehouse automatically backs up its data

questions.explanation: B is correct. When AUTO_RESUME is enabled (default is TRUE), a suspended warehouse automatically starts up when a query is submitted to it. If disabled, the warehouse must be manually resumed before queries can be executed.

questions.question: What is a Resource Monitor in Snowflake used for?

options.text: Monitoring CPU and memory usage of queries
Setting credit usage limits and notifications for warehouses or the account

questions.explanation: B is correct. Resource Monitors track credit usage over a specified interval and can trigger notifications or actions (suspend warehouse, suspend immediately, notify only) when thresholds are reached. They can be set at the account level or on individual warehouses.

questions.question: Which actions can a Resource Monitor trigger when a credit threshold is reached? (Choose two)

options.text: Suspend the warehouse after running queries complete
Delete old data to reduce costs

questions.explanation: A and B are correct. Resource Monitors can send notifications to account administrators, suspend the warehouse (after current queries finish), or suspend immediately (killing running queries). They cannot resize warehouses or delete data.

questions.question: What is the minimum billing increment for a virtual warehouse?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Virtual warehouses have a minimum billing of 60 seconds (1 minute) when they start up. After that initial minute, billing is per-second. This means even a 5-second query will be billed for at least 60 seconds of warehouse time.

questions.question: What is a Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake?

options.text: A physical data center owned by Snowflake
A named abstraction for a cluster of compute resources used to execute queries and DML
A logical container for storing databases
A network load balancer for distributing queries

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Virtual Warehouse is a named cluster of compute resources (CPU, memory, SSD cache) that Snowflake provisions from the cloud provider. It is used to execute SQL queries, load data, and perform DML operations. It is independent of storage.

questions.question: Which Snowflake feature allows you to run queries on data stored in external cloud storage without loading it?
questions.explanation: B is correct. External Tables allow you to query data stored in external cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob, GCS) without loading it into Snowflake. The data remains in the external location, and Snowflake accesses it on demand. External tables are read-only.

questions.question: What is Snowflake's native support for semi-structured data?

options.text: Semi-structured data must be converted to relational format before loading
Snowflake natively stores and queries semi-structured data (JSON, Avro, Parquet, ORC, XML) using the VARIANT data type
Semi-structured data is stored as plain text strings
Snowflake does not support semi-structured data

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake natively supports semi-structured data formats including JSON, Avro, Parquet, ORC, and XML. Data is stored in the VARIANT, OBJECT, or ARRAY data types and can be queried using dot notation and bracket notation.

questions.question: Which data types does Snowflake provide for semi-structured data? (Choose three)
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. VARIANT can hold any type of value including objects and arrays. OBJECT stores key-value pairs (like JSON objects). ARRAY stores ordered lists of values. DOCUMENT and BLOB are not Snowflake semi-structured data types.

questions.question: How does Snowflake handle data encryption in transit?

options.text: Data is not encrypted in transit
TLS 1.2 or higher is required for all connections
Encryption in transit is optional and must be enabled manually

questions.explanation: B is correct. All connections to Snowflake require TLS 1.2 or higher encryption. This is mandatory and cannot be disabled. All data transmitted between clients and Snowflake is encrypted in transit.

questions.question: What is the Snowflake Information Schema?

options.text: A dashboard showing account billing information
A set of system-defined views in each database that provide metadata about objects in that database
A tool for managing user permissions
A staging area for data loading

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Information Schema (INFORMATION_SCHEMA) is a set of system-defined views and table functions available in every database. It provides real-time metadata about database objects, columns, privileges, and usage. Data in Information Schema is typically retained for 14 days.

questions.question: What is the difference between Information Schema and Account Usage?

options.text: Information Schema has real-time data scoped to a database; Account Usage has up to 365 days of data across the entire account with a latency of up to 45 minutes
Account Usage is real-time; Information Schema has a delay
Information Schema is only available on Enterprise edition

questions.explanation: B is correct. Information Schema provides real-time metadata but only for the current database and retains data for 14 days. Account Usage (in the shared SNOWFLAKE database) covers the entire account, retains data for up to 365 days, but has a latency of 45 minutes to 3 hours.

questions.question: Which Snowflake feature enables continuous, serverless data loading from cloud storage?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowpipe enables continuous, serverless data loading. It automatically detects new files in a stage (via cloud event notifications or REST API) and loads them into tables. It uses serverless compute, so no virtual warehouse is needed.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition is the entry-level offering?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Standard is the entry-level edition providing core Snowflake functionality including full SQL support, 1 day of Time Travel, secure data sharing, and all basic features. Enterprise adds features like multi-cluster warehouses, up to 90-day Time Travel, and materialized views.

questions.question: What feature does the Business Critical edition add over Enterprise?

options.text: Enhanced security features including HIPAA/PCI compliance, Tri-Secret Secure, and database failover

questions.explanation: B is correct. Business Critical adds enhanced security and compliance features: HIPAA and PCI DSS compliance, Tri-Secret Secure (customer-managed encryption keys), database failover/failback for disaster recovery, and AWS PrivateLink/Azure Private Link support.

questions.question: What is the Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS) edition?

options.text: The highest level of security with a completely separate Snowflake deployment and dedicated metadata store
A free version for development purposes

questions.explanation: B is correct. VPS provides the highest level of security with a completely separate Snowflake environment. It includes all Business Critical features plus a dedicated metadata store and compute pool, fully isolated from other Snowflake customers.

questions.question: How is Snowflake storage billed?

options.text: Per TB per month based on average daily storage including Time Travel and Fail-safe
A flat rate regardless of data volume
Only when data is actively queried

questions.explanation: B is correct. Storage is billed per TB per month based on the average amount of compressed data stored each day. This includes active data, Time Travel data, and Fail-safe data. Snowflake compresses data automatically, so you pay for the compressed size.

questions.question: Does Snowflake charge for data ingress (loading data into Snowflake)?

options.text: Yes, Snowflake charges for all data ingress
No, Snowflake does not charge for data ingress, but the cloud provider may charge for egress from source
Only for data loaded via Snowpipe

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake does not charge for data ingress. However, data egress (transferring data out of Snowflake to a different region or cloud provider) does incur charges. The source cloud provider may also charge egress fees on their side.

questions.question: What is a Snowflake Account?

options.text: A self-contained environment with its own URL, users, databases, warehouses, and billing

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Snowflake Account is an independent, self-contained environment with its own URL (account_identifier.snowflakecomputing.com), users, roles, databases, warehouses, and separate billing. Accounts exist within a Snowflake Organization.

questions.question: What is a Snowflake Organization?

options.text: A group of users within a single account
A top-level container that links one or more Snowflake accounts for centralized management

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Snowflake Organization is a top-level construct that groups one or more accounts. It enables centralized account management, cross-account data replication, usage tracking across all accounts, and the ability to create new accounts via the ORGADMIN role.

questions.question: Which Snowflake object is used to define the format of data files for loading and unloading?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A File Format object defines the format of data files (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Avro, ORC, XML) including options like delimiters, compression, encoding, and error handling. File Formats can be named objects or specified inline in COPY commands.

questions.question: What are Snowflake Stages used for?

options.text: Staging areas for data files before loading into tables or after unloading from tables
Intermediate compute steps in query processing

questions.explanation: A is correct. Stages are locations (internal or external) where data files are stored for loading into Snowflake tables or unloading from Snowflake tables. Internal stages store files within Snowflake; external stages reference cloud storage locations (S3, Azure Blob, GCS).

questions.question: Which types of internal stages exist in Snowflake? (Choose three)
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. Snowflake has three types of internal stages: User stages (@~, one per user), Table stages (@%table_name, one per table), and Named stages (created with CREATE STAGE). Schema and Database stages do not exist.

questions.question: What is the maximum query timeout limit in Snowflake?
questions.explanation: C is correct. The STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS parameter controls the maximum execution time for a query. The default is 172800 seconds (48 hours). It can be set at the account, user, session, or warehouse level.

questions.question: What is Snowflake's approach to data compression?

options.text: Users must manually specify compression algorithms
Snowflake automatically compresses all stored data and chooses optimal compression
Compression is only applied during data loading

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake automatically compresses all data stored in micro-partitions. The system chooses the optimal compression algorithm for each column based on the data type and content. Users cannot and do not need to specify compression settings for stored data.

questions.question: Which scaling policy determines when to shut down additional clusters in a multi-cluster warehouse?

options.text: Economy — keeps clusters running longer to avoid startup costs
Standard — shuts down clusters quickly when no longer needed
Both Economy and Standard are scaling policies with different shutdown behaviors
Scaling policies only control startup, not shutdown

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both are scaling policies. Standard mode starts clusters quickly and shuts them down as soon as load decreases. Economy mode conserves credits by keeping clusters running longer (waits 5-6 minutes of reduced load) to avoid frequent start/stop cycles.

questions.question: What is the SNOWFLAKE shared database?

options.text: A user-created database that is shared between accounts
A system-provided database containing Account Usage, Organization Usage, and other metadata views
A staging database for data loading
A sample database with demo data

questions.explanation: B is correct. The SNOWFLAKE database is a system-shared database available in every account. It contains schemas like ACCOUNT_USAGE (query history, login history, etc.), ORGANIZATION_USAGE, DATA_SHARING_USAGE, and READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE for monitoring and governance.

questions.question: Can a Snowflake virtual warehouse be resized while it is running?

options.text: No, the warehouse must be suspended first
Yes, resizing takes effect immediately for new queries
Only if no queries are currently running
Only ACCOUNTADMIN can resize running warehouses

questions.explanation: B is correct. Warehouses can be resized while running. The new size takes effect for subsequent queries. Currently running queries may or may not use the additional resources depending on their execution stage.

questions.question: What is a Snowflake Partner Connect?

options.text: A private network connection between Snowflake and on-premises systems
A feature that allows easy integration with third-party tools like Tableau, dbt, and Fivetran directly from the Snowflake UI
A data sharing mechanism between Snowflake partners
A technical support portal for Snowflake partners

questions.explanation: B is correct. Partner Connect provides a streamlined way to create trial accounts and integrate with third-party tools and services (like ETL, BI, ML tools) directly from the Snowsight interface. It simplifies the setup process for partner integrations.

questions.question: How many databases can a single Snowflake account contain?

options.text: There is no hard limit documented; accounts can hold a very large number of databases

questions.explanation: D is correct. Snowflake does not impose a strict hard limit on the number of databases per account. In practice, accounts can contain thousands of databases. Limits are governed by account-level configurations and can be adjusted by Snowflake support if needed.
